top.title: Another 'miracle' in Istanbul - but this one hurt Liverpool
top.description: When it comes to comebacks, Liverpool and Istanbul have plenty of history - but this time Andoni Iraola's side made the wrong kind. Having hit the front for a second time against Fenerbahce, when Alexander Isak nodded in after 69 minutes, Liverpool were seemingly on their way to a thoroughly impressive away win. But Iraola's players then capitulated amid a febrile atmosphere, as spirited hosts led by interim boss Dirk Kuyt - a Liverpool hero of years gone by - pulled off a shock Champions League comeback victory. By losing 3-2 at the Sukru Saracoglu stadium, Iraola's visitors created that unwanted slice of history: this was the latest Liverpool have ever gone ahead in a major European game and then been beaten. Iraola described the goals they conceded as "cheap" and "messy". After Liverpool let three points slip from their grasp, Kuyt spoke of how he had encouraged Fenerbahce's players to embrace the never-say-die mindset that allowed the Reds to achieve so many great feats in Europe in the past. He joined Liverpool in 2006, a year after the team's famous 'Miracle of Istanbul' comeback in the Champions League final, and spent six years at Anfield. "We told each other to stick together and be united. That's something I learned from Liverpool, who we played against," Kuyt said. "We made a miracle tonight - not many expected us to win." He and Fenerbahce will remember this one for a long time. Liverpool will want to quickly forget it. After winning five games in a row, Iraola's side have gone on to lose twice in four days. Arsenal on Sunday, and now this. On their overnight flight back from Istanbul, there will be plenty of disappointment at the way in which Liverpool failed to see this game out. "It's frustration because it's a difficult place to come and play," said Iraola. "We were, during most part of the game, thinking we can win this one. But obviously it hasn't happened." All three of Fenerbahce's goals came from set-pieces. Two were scored by Englishmen. Former Manchester United forward Mason Greenwood benefited from a slice of luck when his free-kick deflected in off Jeremy Jacquet in the first half for Fenerbahce's first equaliser, and Liverpool only had themselves to blame when Cody Gakpo's header took the ball past Alisson and gave Birmingham-born Archie Brown a tap in to make it 2-2. Six minutes later, Liverpool made a mess of Brown's looping ball in the box and Vedat Muriqi beat three players in red and headed past Alisson. "They are cheap goals. They are messy goals," said Iraola. "It's a free-kick. It's quite far also and it's through the wall. "Mistakes can cost you. For the last goal, it's a long throw and the first phase is controlled but after a very long ball, Muriqi wins it. top.description: The hype train is in full motion with No. 1 Miami slated to face off against No. 11 Notre Dame in South Bend on NBC and Peacock this Saturday. Heading into the weekend fresh off the first College Football Playoff rankings release, there's no shortage of storylines for what could be one of the season's most consequential matchups. Ahead of Saturday's highly-anticipated clash, look back at the storied history between both historic programs. How to watch No. 1 Miami vs. No. 11 Notre Dame: TV, live stream, preview for Saturday’s game With major College Football Playoff implications at stake, a storied rivalry will continue with coverage on NBC and Peacock. Nate Ryan , Notre Dame vs. Miami football history, rivalry The Notre Dame Fighting Irish and Miami Hurricanes first clashed helmets over seven decades ago, in 1955. Notre Dame posted a 14-0 victory in what would be the first of 28 meetings between the two schools, and the beginning of a fierce rivalry that heated up in the 1970s and peaked in the late 1980s. While Notre Dame and Miami only faced off only three times during the 1960s, they battled every single year from 1971-1990 (excluding 1986). At first, the Fighting Irish ruled the rivalry with an iron fist, going 12-1-1 against the Hurricanes through 1980. However, this is when the tide began to shift. The Hurricanes would go on to win five of the next six matchups leading up to 1988, when the most famous meeting of the rivalry would occur: the ‘Catholics vs. Convicts’ game. The end of the 1980s also marked a cooling of tensions between the two squads. They only played each other once during the entirety of the 1990s, taking a 20-year hiatus before meeting again in 2010, 2012, 2016, 2017, 2025, and now 2026. The Notre Dame-Miami rivalry was dubbed the ‘Catholics vs. Convicts’ rivalry in the days leading up to their 1988 matchup, due to a T-shirt slogan of the same name made by Notre Dame students. top.title: Ball State football falls to UMass in MACtion overtime heartbreaker
top.description: Ball State football got its midweek MACtion slate started with a brutal road loss. Ball State (3-6, 2-3 MAC) suffered a 31-30 overtime defeat on the road at UMass (5-4, 2-3 MAC) , putting their season on the ropes as far as qualifying for a bowl game. The Cardinals ended a two-game winning streak and are now 1-12 on the road under head coach Mike Uremovich. The Minutemen, meanwhile, snapped a four-game losing streak and earned their first home win over an FBS opponent in 20 games. Ball State executed a two-minute drill to tie the game late in regulation and force overtime at 24-24. The Cardinals got the ball first and scored quickly, but kicker Brody Boehm sent the extra point wide left. UMass scored even quicker, and kicker Derek Morris converted on his extra point to give the Minutemen the victory. More: Ball State football coach Mike Uremovich blasts 24-team CFP, US Congress With six losses on the year, Ball State cannot afford another loss over its final three games in order to reach the six wins required for bowl eligibility. The Cardinals have not made a bowl game since 2021 and have not won one since 2020. Here are three takeaways from Ball State football's road loss to UMass on MACtion. Reemergence of penalties hurts Ball State Ball State has been one of the most penalized teams in the MAC this season with 64 total flags on the year entering MACtion, but the Cardinals appeared to have cleaned things up in that department during their recent two-game winning streak with six penalties against Bowling Green and seven against Sacramento State. The yellow flags reappeared on Wednesday night, as the Cardinals were flagged 10 times for 95 yards. The most damning rash of penalties came on UMass' first touchdown drive, in which the Minutemen drove 80 yards for a touchdown and got 45 of those yards via penalties against the Ball State defense. The offense didn't fare much better with the flags, as the Cardinals consistently found themselves behind the sticks facing third-and-long scenarios. Ball State averaged 9.3 yards to go on third downs, on which they went 6-for-14. Defense wins turnover battle but still leaky UMass entered this matchup with the best turnover margin in the MAC at +7, but it was Ball State who won the turnover battle with two key forced fumbles. Linebacker Mikeah Webster was involved in each one, as he recovered a ball that was stripped by defensive back Gabe Aramboles in the second quarter, then punched out a ball that was recovered by defensive end Ben Marsh in the third quarter. The Cardinals were unable to capitalize on the first turnover, but scored a touchdown two plays after the second one. However, the Cardinals' defense still proved susceptible to giving up explosive plays through the air, which UMass quarterback Pop Watson took advantage of on the Minutemen's scoring drives. top.title: State semifinal ending for DeWitt boys soccer fueled by October meeting
top.description: WATERFORD — Joe Ishraidi sensed a shift was needed. The energy within his DeWitt boys soccer program wasn't sitting well with the 12th year coach. So instead of taking the field for practice the day after their Oct. 7 CAAC Silver Cup finals loss to Mason, the Panthers had a team meeting. They aired things out with players and coaches being brutally honest with each other. And once the coaches left, the players talked on their own led by the seniors. "We wrote a bunch of stuff down on a whiteboard and we all signed it," DeWitt senior goalkeeper Vince Rose said. "I know it's a little cliché, but I think it worked. We started to care for each other and fight for our brothers." That meeting provided the spark for what turned out to be the Panthers' deepest playoff run since reaching the state semifinals in 2021. That tournament run came to an end Wednesday, November 4 with a 3-2 loss to No. 6-ranked Warren De La Salle in a Division 2 state semifinal at Waterford Kettering High School. But despite the ending, the last few weeks proved to Rose, Ishraidi and others in the program what is possible when all are on the same page "I think it just shows the power of guys buying in and being willing to work towards something that's bigger than themselves," Ishraidi said. "I couldn't have said that a month ago. We had a great conversation as a team, and they all decided to start focusing in and work hard in practice and that we're going to execute everything we talk about in practice, It's amazing what can happen when you have 25 guys that buy in." The way the Panthers (13-5-5) came together over the last few weeks was on display in Wednesday's semifinal. DeWitt fell into an early two-goal deficit in the opening 10 minutes. But they kept fighting, scoring a goal in the middle stages of the opening half when Mason Raborn found the back of the net. That fight continued in the second half and DeWitt eventually tied the game at 2 with 4:17 remaining on a goal by freshman Jake Wever. Warren De La Salle broke that tie with a goal with 55 seconds remaining off a corner kick that ultimately led to the end of the road for the Panthers. And while the ending stung, Rose is proud of the journey over the last few weeks that included this year's team adding a layer to DeWitt's postseason success. The Panthers knocked off No. 3-ranked Lansing Eastern in a district final on the way to capturing a third regional title since 2020. DeWitt captured a seventh district title in eight season this fall. "We were kind of the Cinderella story almost," Rose said. "We were underdogs back in (the) district. I'm just really proud of the way we showed up for each other." Contact Brian Calloway at bcalloway@lsj.com. Follow him on X @brian_calloway. top.title: Browns’ Shedeur Sanders appears to send Saints defense a warning with cheeky response
top.description: Photo by Chris Unger/Getty Images Shedeur Sanders appears to have sent a message to the New Orleans Saints defence after delivering a cheeky response when asked about the unit ahead of the Cleveland Browns’ next game. The 24-year-old could be in line for his first start of the 2026 campaign after Deshaun Watson entered the NFL’s concussion protocol. Cleveland are coming off a disappointing 27-6 defeat to the Pittsburgh Steelers, making the quarterback situation an important talking point ahead of their meeting with New Orleans. Shedeur Sanders hints at confidence against New Orleans Saints defence Sanders was asked about the Saints’ defence during his media availability and chose not to give a straightforward assessment. Instead, the Browns quarterback offered a cryptic response that suggested he was feeling confident about the matchup. “Yeah, I’ve seen a lot. When I smile, just know that means something,” Sanders said. He then added: “I’m maturing, you know what I’m saying? I’m maturing. Like, I could have gave that a decent answer, but now I’m just going to smile.” The comments have attracted attention, with Sanders seemingly hinting that he has spotted something he believes Cleveland can exploit. Sanders has spent much of the season watching from the sidelines after losing the starting job to Watson. He has appeared in just two games, completing all three of his pass attempts for two yards. However, he did get an opportunity to start during the second half of Cleveland’s 2025 campaign after initially beginning his rookie season as a backup. His numbers were mixed, completing 120 of 212 passes for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions. Now, with Watson’s availability uncertain, Sanders could have another opportunity to show what he can do as the Browns’ starting quarterback. The Saints’ defence has struggled this season, but Sanders’ comments could give New Orleans extra motivation heading into the contest. Whether he gets the nod remains dependent on Watson’s recovery and clearance from concussion protocol. If Sanders does start, he will have a chance to back up his confident words on the field. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) Maddie Meyer BOSTON (AP) — Paul George scored 25 points and had five 3-pointers, Derrick White added 24 points and seven assists, and the Boston Celtics beat the Milwaukee Bucks 109-102 on Wednesday night. Tyler Herro scored 18 of his 25 points during the third quarter for the Bucks, who fell to 1-7, including 0-4 on the road. Jaime Jaquez Jr. added 18 points. Baylor Scheierman had nine points and 11 rebounds off the bench for the Celtics, who survived a scare after being pushed by one of the NBA’s weaker teams. Boston never trailed through three quarters, opening a 22-point advantage in the second quarter, leading by 21 at halftime and eight entering the fourth. Milwaukee’s best stretch came during the third quarter, with a 26-12 run to make it a single-digit game. When Ryan Rollins slammed home two of his 13 points, the Bucks trailed 91-89 with 8:17 remaining. George threw the ball away coming out of a timeout, with Milwaukee’s Nate Ament racing the other way for a layup that tied it at 91. The Bucks took their first lead of the game at 92-91 when Ament hit a free throw. With leading scorer Jayson Tatum watching from the bench, and Payton Pritchard missing the final quarter with what the team called a right eye abrasion, the Celtics’ search for late-game offense was answered when White converted a hoop-and-harm sequence that put Boston up 102-97 with 2:22 left. Boston outscored Milwaukee 12-5 over the final three minutes. The Celtics shot 41% from three (16 of 39) and improved to 5-0 at home. Tatum (rest) was sidelined for Boston for the first time this season. The All-Star forward was coming off a 19-point game during Monday’s 109-93 loss to the Houston Rockets. top.description: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images Just two weeks into the 2026-27 NBA season, the league landscape has flipped. Injuries and surprise surges have changed the standings. The Houston Rockets sit at number one with a 7-1 record. Meanwhile, the defending champion New York Knicks start 0-3 and fight to get back in the top tier. The West is heating up as teams like the Oklahoma City Thunder deal with injuries to stars. This early stretch shows that depth matters more than ever. The Houston Rockets have found their rhythm. Fred VanVleet returned from a season-ending knee injury to lead the team. His impact is clear. Houston now has the league’s best offense rating at 121.2. They added Marcus Smart as a backup to handle the second night of back-to-back games. The team is calmer and more organized. They moved the ball well and limited turnovers. This is what a good floor general does for a squad. Young Cores Take Over in the West Memphis is proving that youth can win right now. The Grizzlies started 6-1. They moved Ja Morant in June and pivoted to a younger build. GM Zach Kleiman said this shift was “not going to be some drawn-out five-year process.” He was right. Young players like Cameron Boozer and Cedric Coward are taking major roles. Ty Jerome has made an early impact. The team is fast and energetic. They do not need a veteran star to start strong. The Minnesota Timberwolves face a different test. They deal with injuries to their stars. This opens the door for others to step up. Rudy Gobert is playing well in some ways, but his shooting has been a problem. Over a two-game span, he missed all 13 field goal attempts. He also blocked only four shots in seven games. top.title: Xavier edges Wilbur Cross to capture eighth SCC boys soccer championship
top.description: Xavier head coach Brian Fitzgerald and team celebrate after defeating Wilbur Cross 2-1 in the SCC Boys Soccer Final at West Haven High School in West Haven, Conn., Wednesday, November 4, 2026. (Dave Zajac/Hearst Connecticut Media) WEST HAVEN - When Rays Kisaku came to Xavier, he said he promised something to his boys soccer coach. "I told my coach (Brian Fitzgerald) I would win it (a championship) for him," Kisaku said. It took three seasons, but Kisaku cashed in on that promise. He scored in the early stages of the second half, the game-winning goal, for top seed Xavier in a 2-1 victory over No. 3 Wilbur Cross Wednesday at Ken Strong Stadium. The Falcons (17-0-2), the No. 2 team in the GametimeCT rankings , won their eighth SCC championship, fifth in this decade alone. After winning four straight from 2020-23, Xavier missed out the last two seasons. "It's a goal every season to win the division, win the conference and win states," Fitzgerald said. "We tell the guys from the get-go, they know the expectations are high. They work, they work for it. We hold them to a high standard and every year that culture doesn't change, that standard doesn't change." This was the first appearance in an SCC championship game for Wilbur Cross (14-3-2). The Governors salvaged a 1-1 tie with Xavier during the regular season. "It's bittersweet because we came here to win. The kids battled their rear ends off," Wilbur Cross coach Scott Raffone said. "I'm so proud of them, so proud of the effort." Kisaku scored just 1 minute, 26 seconds into the second half. John Staron, who scored Xavier's tying goal, had the initial shot. Wilbur Cross goalkeeper Luis Rodriguez kept the Governors in it with eight saves. One of those came on Staron's shot. But Rodriguez could not control it. "Whenever he shoots, I kind of just run for it. I always know it's going to be on frame, so on that play I saw it, the keeper is bound to deflect it," Kisaku said. "From then, I just chased it down and put it in the back of the net." Kisaku believed the defense would hold up and the Falcons proved him right. Xavier goalkeeper Roldofo Fraschilla was named the SCC tournament Most Outstanding Player. He allowed just the one first-half goal to Wilbur Cross in the three-game tournament. "They pressured us in a way where I was on my toes until the very last second," Fraschilla said. "At no point did I let my guard down. "I was always on high alert. I don't play this sport for awards, I play it for my team. I'm so proud of these guys. This group of very accomplished players, I can't wait to see where all their careers take them." Leo Castellano scored the opening goal for Wilbur Cross off a direct kick. Player of the Game Rays Kisaku, Xavier: Junior buried the rebound off an initial shot to put Xavier ahead to stay, 2-1 in the second half. Quotable "A hard-fought win against a quality opponent like Wilbur Cross is great." -Xavier soccer coach Brian Fitzgerald Xavier 2, Wilbur Cross 1 (at West Haven) W. C

top.title: Sixers roll on to down Pistons, Knicks gore Bulls
top.description: Jaylen Brown's 30-point performance helped Philadelphia down the Detroit Pistons in their top-of-the-table Eastern Conference duel on Wednesday (Gregory Shamus) Jaylen Brown and Joel Embiid combined for 56 points as the Philadelphia 76ers defeated the Detroit Pistons 112-106 in their heavyweight top-of-the-table NBA Eastern Conference clash on Wednesday. Brown finished with 30 points and Embiid added 26 to give the Sixers another impressive road win that moved them to 8-1 at the top of the standings, with Detroit (6-2) in second. Brown and Embiid led another balanced offensive performance from Philadelphia, who saw all five starters reach double figures. LeBron James added a double-double with 13 points, 10 rebounds and eight assists while Tyrese Maxey drained three three-pointers on his way to a 19-point haul. Brown, who arrived from the Boston Celtics in the offseason, said he was "still adjusting" to his new team-mates. "I'm still figuring it out," Brown said, before paying tribute to the performance of 41-year-old team-mate James. "LeBron has been great," Brown said. "To see what he's doing at his age makes sense for LeBron James, but for nobody else would it make sense." The Sixers moved into the lead towards the end of the first quarter and kept their noses in front for the remainder of the game, stretching the lead to 18 points before a late rally from Detroit. Duncan Robinson led the Pistons with 27 points while Cade Cunningham added 26. The reigning champion New York Knicks scored their biggest win of the season with a 135-105 blowout over the Chicago Bulls at Madison Square Garden. The Knicks, who have made a slow start to the new campaign, improved to 4-4 after a dazzling 33-point performance from Jalen Brunson, who drained five three-pointers while making 10-of-17 from the field. O.G. Anunoby scored 18 points while Karl-Anthony Towns added 17 for a Knicks team who led by as many as 44 points midway through the third quarter. In Boston, the Milwaukee Bucks threatened to pull off a huge comeback before finally succumbing 109-102 to the Celtics. Paul George (25 points) and Derrick White (24) led the scoring for Boston, who appeared to be cruising after leading by 20 early in the third quarter. But a 38-point third quarter from Milwaukee flipped the script and the Bucks edged into a 96-95 lead with five minutes remaining. Boston regained control down the stretch with George and White closing out the win. rcw/pst

nigeria.description: … Women record twice men’s prevalence as state targets wider coverage By Chioma Obinna Lagos State has recorded significant progress in HIV treatment, with 93.4 per cent of people living with the virus who know their status receiving antiretroviral therapy (ART), a new survey has revealed. However, only 58.3 per cent of people living with HIV know their status, highlighting a major testing gap that could undermine efforts to control the epidemic. The 2025–2026 Antiretroviral Therapy (ART) Impact Survey also found that HIV prevalence among adults aged 15 to 64 was twice as high among women as men, at 1.6 per cent and 0.8 per cent, respectively. nigeria.title: Nasarawa APC crisis: Govt calls for probe of rally disruption
nigeria.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia The Nasarawa State Government has called on security agencies to investigate an incident that reportedly disrupted activities surrounding Vice-President Kashim Shettima’s visit to the Emir of Lafia during Wednesday’s All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally. The government made the call following reports of disturbances during the Vice-President’s visit to the traditional ruler and allegations of an incident involving Governor Abdullahi Sule at the rally held at Lafia Square. The governor’s Personal Assistant on Social Media, Emmanuel Innocent Akwe, had raised concerns over the incident, alleging that the governor was pelted with objects suspected to be stones by some aggrieved party members. In a statement, Akwe described the reported incident as unacceptable and called for respect for the office of the governor and the unity of the APC in the state. The state government subsequently expressed concern over the reported disruption of the Vice-President’s visit to the Emir, urging security agencies to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident. The Secretary to the State Government, Labaran Magaji, who made the government’s position known in a statement, said Shettima had visited the traditional ruler as a mark of respect for the traditional institution. He regretted that the visit was reportedly disrupted by actions he described as disrespectful to constituted authorities and the office of the Vice-President. Magaji urged security agencies to conduct a thorough investigation, identify those responsible for any wrongdoing and ensure that anyone found culpable was dealt with in accordance with the law. The development comes amid political disagreements within the state chapter of the APC following the party’s recent governorship primary. However, the circumstances surrounding the reported disturbances and the identities of those responsible have yet to be independently established. As of the time of filing this report, there had been no official clarification on the allegations surrounding the incidents. nigeria.title: Google turns off AI for schoolchildren by default
nigeria.description: Google has said it will switch off its AI tools for schoolchildren by default, after drawing criticism for pushing artificial intelligence features to students while schools are still debating how the technology should be used in classrooms. The search engine juggernaut dominates technology in American schools. Its education apps, including Gmail, Docs and the Classroom platform, are used in classrooms across the country, and its low-cost Chromebook laptops are the devices US schools most often issue to students. Under the changes Google announced in a blog post on Tuesday, Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom and Search will be turned off for K-12 student accounts until school administrators switch them on. Google told AFP the new controls would be rolled out worldwide, beginning in the United States, but that it had not yet set a date. The changes also mean schools will not be able to give students Google Search without its AI features. Chris Phillips, Google’s vice president for education, told The New York Times that “Search and A.I. are deeply integrated,” as AI features are now built into the company’s search engine. If a school bans AI, he said, students “will not have access to search, and they’ll see a message from their school that indicates it’s not available.” New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani accused Google on X of “trying to use its monopoly power to force AI into our public schools.” “No corporation should have the power to dictate how we teach our children,” he wrote. More than 150 million students worldwide use Google Classroom, according to a letter Senators Richard Blumenthal and Josh Hawley sent to the company last month asking why AI features had been made the default on school devices. In August, Google opened its Gemini chatbot in Classroom to students of all ages. entertainment.title: African Philanthropy Leaders Call for Bolder, Locally Led Giving at the 2026 APF Conference in Cape Town
entertainment.description: CAPE TOWN, South Africa: African Philanthropy Forum (APF) closed its 2026 Conference in Cape Town on 27 October with a message that ran through nearly every session: Africa’s challenges are connected, so African giving has to be connected too. Held from 25 to 27 October under the theme Bridge the Divide; Reimagine the Future , the conference brought together philanthropists, funders, business leaders, creatives, and technologists to ask how African capital can be mobilized, how partnerships can be strengthened, and how African-led solutions can be backed with more trust and flexibility. Centered on Africa, the program also looked outward, drawing on solutions from across the Global South and asking how African philanthropy can bridge the divide. The conference opened on Sunday evening with a reception at Cape Point Vineyards, where Executive Director Mosun Layode welcomed delegates, members and acknowledged APF Board members, including Chair Gbenga Oyebode , Wale Adeosun , and Nyimpini Mabunda . Former Board Member Phuthi Mahanyele-Dabengwa urged guests to look past the continent’s challenges and toward its potential and to use the days ahead to turn conversations into partnerships. It was an evening of connection before two days of ideas at the Norval Foundation. Reimagining the Future Monday, 26 October, began with a call to build bridges across regions, languages, and funding silos. Mosun Layode and Gbenga Oyebode officially opened and welcomed all delegates to the conference. Dr. Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka , former Vice President of South Africa, spoke of education as a sacred right of every African child and of bringing young people into decision-making. In the first keynote, Gary Lubner, Founder of the This Day Foundation, described giving away 95 percent of his wealth during his lifetime and said it was easier and more joyful than holding it for heirs. Old money thinking, he argued, is a major barrier to giving, and generosity includes time and effort as well as cash. The numbers framed the challenge. Delegates heard that Africa needs about $1.3 trillion in financing each year, while philanthropy contributes $5 billion to $6 billion. The task is to use that small pool to unlock far larger sources, such as pension funds and fixed-income assets, so money reaches businesses that create jobs. In an afternoon keynote moderated by Marlene Ogawa of Synergos, Phuthi Mahanyele-Dabengwa , South Africa CEO of Naspers, and Gareth Ackerman, Non-Executive Director at Pick n Pay, kept things practical: back women entrepreneurs without taking equity, start with your own family and community, use local distributors, and make it easier to travel between African countries. One retraining program they discussed moved 7,200 of 8,000 university graduates into tech jobs. The difference between charity and philanthropy, they said, is helping people help themselves. sports.title: Another 'miracle' in Istanbul - but this one hurt Liverpool
sports.description: When it comes to comebacks, Liverpool and Istanbul have plenty of history - but this time Andoni Iraola's side made the wrong kind. Having hit the front for a second time against Fenerbahce, when Alexander Isak nodded in after 69 minutes, Liverpool were seemingly on their way to a thoroughly impressive away win. But Iraola's players then capitulated amid a febrile atmosphere, as spirited hosts led by interim boss Dirk Kuyt - a Liverpool hero of years gone by - pulled off a shock Champions League comeback victory. By losing 3-2 at the Sukru Saracoglu stadium, Iraola's visitors created that unwanted slice of history: this was the latest Liverpool have ever gone ahead in a major European game and then been beaten. Iraola described the goals they conceded as "cheap" and "messy". After Liverpool let three points slip from their grasp, Kuyt spoke of how he had encouraged Fenerbahce's players to embrace the never-say-die mindset that allowed the Reds to achieve so many great feats in Europe in the past. He joined Liverpool in 2006, a year after the team's famous 'Miracle of Istanbul' comeback in the Champions League final, and spent six years at Anfield. "We told each other to stick together and be united. That's something I learned from Liverpool, who we played against," Kuyt said. "We made a miracle tonight - not many expected us to win." He and Fenerbahce will remember this one for a long time. Liverpool will want to quickly forget it. After winning five games in a row, Iraola's side have gone on to lose twice in four days. Arsenal on Sunday, and now this. On their overnight flight back from Istanbul, there will be plenty of disappointment at the way in which Liverpool failed to see this game out. "It's frustration because it's a difficult place to come and play," said Iraola. "We were, during most part of the game, thinking we can win this one. But obviously it hasn't happened." All three of Fenerbahce's goals came from set-pieces. Two were scored by Englishmen. sports.description: The hype train is in full motion with No. 1 Miami slated to face off against No. 11 Notre Dame in South Bend on NBC and Peacock this Saturday. Nate Ryan , Notre Dame vs. Miami football history, rivalry The Notre Dame Fighting Irish and Miami Hurricanes first clashed helmets over seven decades ago, in 1955. Notre Dame posted a 14-0 victory in what would be the first of 28 meetings between the two schools, and the beginning of a fierce rivalry that heated up in the 1970s and peaked in the late 1980s. While Notre Dame and Miami only faced off only three times during the 1960s, they battled every single year from 1971-1990 (excluding 1986). At first, the Fighting Irish ruled the rivalry with an iron fist, going 12-1-1 against the Hurricanes through 1980. However, this is when the tide began to shift. The Hurricanes would go on to win five of the next six matchups leading up to 1988, when the most famous meeting of the rivalry would occur: the ‘Catholics vs. Convicts’ game. The end of the 1980s also marked a cooling of tensions between the two squads. They only played each other once during the entirety of the 1990s, taking a 20-year hiatus before meeting again in 2010, 2012, 2016, 2017, 2025, and now 2026. sports.title: Ball State football falls to UMass in MACtion overtime heartbreaker
sports.description: Ball State football got its midweek MACtion slate started with a brutal road loss. Ball State (3-6, 2-3 MAC) suffered a 31-30 overtime defeat on the road at UMass (5-4, 2-3 MAC) , putting their season on the ropes as far as qualifying for a bowl game. The Cardinals ended a two-game winning streak and are now 1-12 on the road under head coach Mike Uremovich. The Minutemen, meanwhile, snapped a four-game losing streak and earned their first home win over an FBS opponent in 20 games. Ball State executed a two-minute drill to tie the game late in regulation and force overtime at 24-24. The Cardinals got the ball first and scored quickly, but kicker Brody Boehm sent the extra point wide left. UMass scored even quicker, and kicker Derek Morris converted on his extra point to give the Minutemen the victory. More: Ball State football coach Mike Uremovich blasts 24-team CFP, US Congress With six losses on the year, Ball State cannot afford another loss over its final three games in order to reach the six wins required for bowl eligibility. The Cardinals have not made a bowl game since 2021 and have not won one since 2020. Here are three takeaways from Ball State football's road loss to UMass on MACtion. Reemergence of penalties hurts Ball State Ball State has been one of the most penalized teams in the MAC this season with 64 total flags on the year entering MACtion, but the Cardinals appeared to have cleaned things up in that department during their recent two-game winning streak with six penalties against Bowling Green and seven against Sacramento State. The yellow flags reappeared on Wednesday night, as the Cardinals were flagged 10 times for 95 yards. The most damning rash of penalties came on UMass' first touchdown drive, in which the Minutemen drove 80 yards for a touchdown and got 45 of those yards via penalties against the Ball State defense. The offense didn't fare much better with the flags, as the Cardinals consistently found themselves behind the sticks facing third-and-long scenarios. Ball State averaged 9.3 yards to go on third downs, on which they went 6-for-14. Defense wins turnover battle but still leaky UMass entered this matchup with the best turnover margin in the MAC at +7, but it was Ball State who won the turnover battle with two key forced fumbles. Linebacker Mikeah Webster was involved in each one, as he recovered a ball that was stripped by defensive back Gabe Aramboles in the second quarter, then punched out a ball that was recovered by defensive end Ben Marsh in the third quarter. The Cardinals were unable to capitalize on the first turnover, but scored a touchdown two plays after the second one. However, the Cardinals' defense still proved susceptible to giving up explosive plays through the air, which UMass quarterback Pop Watson took advantage of on the Minutemen's scoring drives. He threw a 64-yard touchdown just before halftime, then made throws of 46 and 41 yards on back-to-back plays to set up a 1-yard rushing touchdown

With over a minute left in the first quarter, Jarrett Allen appeared to sustain a knee injury after a collision with Thunder guard Jared McCain. sports.description: Oct 17, 2026; Miami Gardens, Florida, USA; Miami Hurricanes wide receiver Malachi Toney (1) warms up before a game against the Florida State Seminoles at Hard Rock Stadium. But the Hurricanes are now heading into their biggest game of the year without their best offensive player. Star wide receiver Malachi Toney suffered an ankle injury at practice on Wednesday, and it has since been revealed that he will need surgery to repair the injury. He’s reportedly set to miss Saturday’s top-15 showdown against Notre Dame, though there’s hope that he could return in time for the College Football Playoff. Toney Injured at Practice Miami’s Wednesday practice was supposed to be just another day of preparation for Notre Dame. Instead, the Hurricanes’ star wideout went down, putting his status for the game in serious doubt . According to On3’s Brett McMurphy, Toney rolled his ankle after getting caught up in a play with a cornerback. Miami confirmed the injury in a statement shortly after. “Malachi Toney sustained an injury during Wednesday’s practice and is currently undergoing further evaluation by the team’s medical staff,” Miami said in a statement, via On3 . “We will share additional updates as appropriate.” Needless to say, losing Toney would be a massive blow for the Hurricanes. The sophomore has 73 catches, the most among Power 4 receivers, for 1,027 yards and 13 touchdowns this season. Toney was just as productive as a freshman last season, leading the FBS with 109 catches and setting a Miami single-season record with 1,211 receiving yards as the Hurricanes reached the national championship game. sports.title: State semifinal ending for DeWitt boys soccer fueled by October meeting
sports.description: WATERFORD — Joe Ishraidi sensed a shift was needed. The energy within his DeWitt boys soccer program wasn't sitting well with the 12th year coach. So instead of taking the field for practice the day after their Oct. 7 CAAC Silver Cup finals loss to Mason, the Panthers had a team meeting. They aired things out with players and coaches being brutally honest with each other. And once the coaches left, the players talked on their own led by the seniors. "We wrote a bunch of stuff down on a whiteboard and we all signed it," DeWitt senior goalkeeper Vince Rose said. "I know it's a little cliché, but I think it worked. We started to care for each other and fight for our brothers." That meeting provided the spark for what turned out to be the Panthers' deepest playoff run since reaching the state semifinals in 2021. That tournament run came to an end Wednesday, November 4 with a 3-2 loss to No. 6-ranked Warren De La Salle in a Division 2 state semifinal at Waterford Kettering High School. But despite the ending, the last few weeks proved to Rose, Ishraidi and others in the program what is possible when all are on the same page "I think it just shows the power of guys buying in and being willing to work towards something that's bigger than themselves," Ishraidi said. "I couldn't have said that a month ago. We had a great conversation as a team, and they all decided to start focusing in and work hard in practice and that we're going to execute everything we talk about in practice, It's amazing what can happen when you have 25 guys that buy in." The way the Panthers (13-5-5) came together over the last few weeks was on display in Wednesday's semifinal. DeWitt fell into an early two-goal deficit in the opening 10 minutes. But they kept fighting, scoring a goal in the middle stages of the opening half when Mason Raborn found the back of the net. That fight continued in the second half and DeWitt eventually tied the game at 2 with 4:17 remaining on a goal by freshman Jake Wever. Warren De La Salle broke that tie with a goal with 55 seconds remaining off a corner kick that ultimately led to the end of the road for the Panthers. And while the ending stung, Rose is proud of the journey over the last few weeks that included this year's team adding a layer to DeWitt's postseason success. The Panthers knocked off No. 3-ranked Lansing Eastern in a district final on the way to capturing a third regional title since 2020. DeWitt captured a seventh district title in eight season this fall. "We were kind of the Cinderella story almost," Rose said. "We were underdogs back in (the) district. I'm just really proud of the way we showed up for each other." Contact Brian Calloway at bcalloway@lsj.com. Follow him on X @brian_calloway. sports.title: Browns’ Shedeur Sanders appears to send Saints defense a warning with cheeky response
sports.description: Photo by Chris Unger/Getty Images Shedeur Sanders appears to have sent a message to the New Orleans Saints defence after delivering a cheeky response when asked about the unit ahead of the Cleveland Browns’ next game. The 24-year-old could be in line for his first start of the 2026 campaign after Deshaun Watson entered the NFL’s concussion protocol. Cleveland are coming off a disappointing 27-6 defeat to the Pittsburgh Steelers, making the quarterback situation an important talking point ahead of their meeting with New Orleans. Shedeur Sanders hints at confidence against New Orleans Saints defence Sanders was asked about the Saints’ defence during his media availability and chose not to give a straightforward assessment. Instead, the Browns quarterback offered a cryptic response that suggested he was feeling confident about the matchup. “Yeah, I’ve seen a lot. When I smile, just know that means something,” Sanders said. He then added: “I’m maturing, you know what I’m saying? I’m maturing. Like, I could have gave that a decent answer, but now I’m just going to smile.” The comments have attracted attention, with Sanders seemingly hinting that he has spotted something he believes Cleveland can exploit. Sanders has spent much of the season watching from the sidelines after losing the starting job to Watson. He has appeared in just two games, completing all three of his pass attempts for two yards. However, he did get an opportunity to start during the second half of Cleveland’s 2025 campaign after initially beginning his rookie season as a backup. His numbers were mixed, completing 120 of 212 passes for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions. Now, with Watson’s availability uncertain, Sanders could have another opportunity to show what he can do as the Browns’ starting quarterback. The Saints’ defence has struggled this season, but Sanders’ comments could give New Orleans extra motivation heading into the contest. Whether he gets the nod remains dependent on Watson’s recovery and clearance from concussion protocol. If Sanders does start, he will have a chance to back up his confident words on the field. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) Maddie Meyer BOSTON (AP) — Paul George scored 25 points and had five 3-pointers, Derrick White added 24 points and seven assists, and the Boston Celtics beat the Milwaukee Bucks 109-102 on Wednesday night. Tyler Herro scored 18 of his 25 points during the third quarter for the Bucks, who fell to 1-7, including 0-4 on the road. Jaime Jaquez Jr. added 18 points. Baylor Scheierman had nine points and 11 rebounds off the bench for the Celtics, who survived a scare after being pushed by one of the NBA’s weaker teams. Boston never trailed through three quarters, opening a 22-point advantage in the second quarter, leading by 21 at halftime and eight entering the fourth. Milwaukee’s best stretch came during the third quarter, with a 26-12 run to make it a single-digit game. When Ryan Rollins slammed home two of his 13 points, the Bucks trailed 91-89 with 8:17 remaining. George threw the ball away coming out of a timeout, with Milwaukee’s Nate Ament racing the other way for a layup that tied it at 91. The Bucks took their first lead of the game at 92-91 when Ament hit a free throw. With leading scorer Jayson Tatum watching from the bench, and Payton Pritchard missing the final quarter with what the team called a right eye abrasion, the Celtics’ search for late-game offense was answered when White converted a hoop-and-harm sequence that put Boston up 102-97 with 2:22 left. Boston outscored Milwaukee 12-5 over the final three minutes. The Celtics shot 41% from three (16 of 39) and improved to 5-0 at home. Tatum (rest) was sidelined for Boston for the first time this season. The All-Star forward was coming off a 19-point game during Monday’s 109-93 loss to the Houston Rockets. sports.title: Power Rankings Shift as Injuries and Upstarts Reshape the NBA
sports.description: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images Just two weeks into the 2026-27 NBA season, the league landscape has flipped. Injuries and surprise surges have changed the standings. The Houston Rockets sit at number one with a 7-1 record. Meanwhile, the defending champion New York Knicks start 0-3 and fight to get back in the top tier. The West is heating up as teams like the Oklahoma City Thunder deal with injuries to stars. This early stretch shows that depth matters more than ever. The Houston Rockets have found their rhythm. Fred VanVleet returned from a season-ending knee injury to lead the team. His impact is clear. Houston now has the league’s best offense rating at 121.2. They added Marcus Smart as a backup to handle the second night of back-to-back games. The team is calmer and more organized. They moved the ball well and limited turnovers. This is what a good floor general does for a squad. Young Cores Take Over in the West Memphis is proving that youth can win right now. The Grizzlies started 6-1. They moved Ja Morant in June and pivoted to a younger build. GM Zach Kleiman said this shift was “not going to be some drawn-out five-year process.” He was right. Young players like Cameron Boozer and Cedric Coward are taking major roles. Ty Jerome has made an early impact. The team is fast and energetic. They do not need a veteran star to start strong. The Minnesota Timberwolves face a different test. They deal with injuries to their stars. This opens the door for others to step up. Rudy Gobert is playing well in some ways, but his shooting has been a problem. Over a two-game span, he missed all 13 field goal attempts. He also blocked only four shots in seven games. Eric Karabell, a senior writer at ESPN , noted that he invested in Gobert because he expected consistency. “Part of the reason I invested in Minnesota Timberwolves C Rudy Gobert… was so I would not have to deal with uncertainty,” Karabell wrote. Gobert is 34 and has done the same thing for a decade. The back injury might explain the poor shooting. He missed layups that he usually makes. Managers should be patient, but the stats show a slump. Knicks Struggle While Stars Shine Elsewhere The New York Knicks are in a tough spot. They started the season 0-3. They are trying to claw their way back. The team needs to find a way to win. Mikal Bridges has been quiet. He attempted zero free throws through 90 minutes. That is unusual for a star. The team needs more from its leaders. Karl-Anthony Towns and Jalen Brunson are top fantasy players, but the team record shows they are not winning enough. The pressure is on to turn things around fast. Luka Doncic is making an early MVP case for the Los Angeles Lakers. He scored 42 and 45 points in his past two games. He does not seem to be slowing down. His name is high on the points rankings. He is the second-ranked player in fantasy points leagues. The Lakers have a new look with him leading the charge. He is scoring at a rate that few can match. This is a big deal

sports.title: Xavier edges Wilbur Cross to capture eighth SCC boys soccer championship
sports.description: Xavier head coach Brian Fitzgerald and team celebrate after defeating Wilbur Cross 2-1 in the SCC Boys Soccer Final at West Haven High School in West Haven, Conn., Wednesday, November 4, 2026. (Dave Zajac/Hearst Connecticut Media) WEST HAVEN - When Rays Kisaku came to Xavier, he said he promised something to his boys soccer coach. "I told my coach (Brian Fitzgerald) I would win it (a championship) for him," Kisaku said. It took three seasons, but Kisaku cashed in on that promise. He scored in the early stages of the second half, the game-winning goal, for top seed Xavier in a 2-1 victory over No. 3 Wilbur Cross Wednesday at Ken Strong Stadium. The Falcons (17-0-2), the No. 2 team in the GametimeCT rankings , won their eighth SCC championship, fifth in this decade alone. After winning four straight from 2020-23, Xavier missed out the last two seasons. "It's a goal every season to win the division, win the conference and win states," Fitzgerald said. "We tell the guys from the get-go, they know the expectations are high. They work, they work for it. We hold them to a high standard and every year that culture doesn't change, that standard doesn't change." This was the first appearance in an SCC championship game for Wilbur Cross (14-3-2). The Governors salvaged a 1-1 tie with Xavier during the regular season. "It's bittersweet because we came here to win. The kids battled their rear ends off," Wilbur Cross coach Scott Raffone said. "I'm so proud of them, so proud of the effort." Kisaku scored just 1 minute, 26 seconds into the second half. John Staron, who scored Xavier's tying goal, had the initial shot. Wilbur Cross goalkeeper Luis Rodriguez kept the Governors in it with eight saves. One of those came on Staron's shot. But Rodriguez could not control it. "Whenever he shoots, I kind of just run for it. I always know it's going to be on frame, so on that play I saw it, the keeper is bound to deflect it," Kisaku said. "From then, I just chased it down and put it in the back of the net." Kisaku believed the defense would hold up and the Falcons proved him right. Xavier goalkeeper Roldofo Fraschilla was named the SCC tournament Most Outstanding Player. He allowed just the one first-half goal to Wilbur Cross in the three-game tournament. "They pressured us in a way where I was on my toes until the very last second," Fraschilla said. "At no point did I let my guard down. "I was always on high alert. I don't play this sport for awards, I play it for my team. I'm so proud of these guys. This group of very accomplished players, I can't wait to see where all their careers take them." Leo Castellano scored the opening goal for Wilbur Cross off a direct kick. Player of the Game Rays Kisaku, Xavier: Junior buried the rebound off an initial shot to put Xavier ahead to stay, 2-1 in the second half. sports.title: Sixers roll on to down Pistons, Knicks gore Bulls
sports.description: Jaylen Brown's 30-point performance helped Philadelphia down the Detroit Pistons in their top-of-the-table Eastern Conference duel on Wednesday (Gregory Shamus) Jaylen Brown and Joel Embiid combined for 56 points as the Philadelphia 76ers defeated the Detroit Pistons 112-106 in their heavyweight top-of-the-table NBA Eastern Conference clash on Wednesday. Brown finished with 30 points and Embiid added 26 to give the Sixers another impressive road win that moved them to 8-1 at the top of the standings, with Detroit (6-2) in second. Brown and Embiid led another balanced offensive performance from Philadelphia, who saw all five starters reach double figures. LeBron James added a double-double with 13 points, 10 rebounds and eight assists while Tyrese Maxey drained three three-pointers on his way to a 19-point haul. Brown, who arrived from the Boston Celtics in the offseason, said he was "still adjusting" to his new team-mates. "I'm still figuring it out," Brown said, before paying tribute to the performance of 41-year-old team-mate James. "LeBron has been great," Brown said. "To see what he's doing at his age makes sense for LeBron James, but for nobody else would it make sense." The Sixers moved into the lead towards the end of the first quarter and kept their noses in front for the remainder of the game, stretching the lead to 18 points before a late rally from Detroit. Duncan Robinson led the Pistons with 27 points while Cade Cunningham added 26. The reigning champion New York Knicks scored their biggest win of the season with a 135-105 blowout over the Chicago Bulls at Madison Square Garden. The Knicks, who have made a slow start to the new campaign, improved to 4-4 after a dazzling 33-point performance from Jalen Brunson, who drained five three-pointers while making 10-of-17 from the field. O.G. Anunoby scored 18 points while Karl-Anthony Towns added 17 for a Knicks team who led by as many as 44 points midway through the third quarter. In Boston, the Milwaukee Bucks threatened to pull off a huge comeback before finally succumbing 109-102 to the Celtics. Paul George (25 points) and Derrick White (24) led the scoring for Boston, who appeared to be cruising after leading by 20 early in the third quarter. But a 38-point third quarter from Milwaukee flipped the script and the Bucks edged into a 96-95 lead with five minutes remaining. Boston regained control down the stretch with George and White closing out the win. rcw/pst

sports.title: How Gabby Williams made the Valkyries' parade a true Bay Area party
sports.description: Golden State Valkyries' Gabby Williams, center, waves to fans along the The Embarcadero during the team's WNBA Championship parade in San Francisco, Wednesday, Nov. 4, 2026. (Santiago Mejia/S.F. Chronicle) The Golden State Valkyries were aboard their double-decker buses. Champagne bottles chilled and ready to pop. Boxes of Valkyries T-shirts and beaded necklaces stacked to give away to the thousands of fans who showed up to party with the newly minted WNBA champions. This championship parade, though, would have to wait a few minutes. As Veronica Burton 's bus - shared with Kaitlyn Chen and Laeticia Amihere - turned the corner out of the Ferry Building and onto the Embarcadero, the procession came to an abrupt stop. It wouldn't be a Bay Area event without a little traffic jam. Luckily, whoever was in charge gave this bus a microphone and speaker, and the volume turned up high enough to reach fans far behind the barricades. Chen grabbed the microphone and asked the crowd a question. "Do you want to hear Veronica Burton sing?" she said. The crowd cheered. Burton, of course, wasn't up for singing. Once traffic got moving and the parade began under clouds of confetti and a shining autumn sun, Burton took the microphone and gave a shout-out to the screaming fans who showed up. To one onlooker, she said, "You have such a cute baby!" The procession rolled through throngs of supporters who perfectly exemplified this Valkyries fan base - one that brought all the signage, enthusiasm, music and get-ups. A crowd of people who showed just how much they fell in love with this team that treated them to a title in its second year of existence. Signs popped up written in French for Gabby Williams , Janelle Salaün and Aminata Gueye; a few were in Italian for Cecilia Zandalasini . Outnumbering those signs but double were ones that read some variation of "For the Gays," a battle cry Williams created this June that stuck. Fans brought their kids, who screamed for their favorite players from the barricades. Many showed off their drawings of all the players. A handful wore hot dog costumes, a nod to Chen arriving at Game 7 on Halloween dressed as a hot dog. Other signs popped up in response to the Democratic takeover of Congress in the prior night's elections - one read "Blue wave + Valkyries parade = fire." Meanwhile, most fans couldn't help but shake their hair and dance when floats rolled by playing Bay Area hits like "Tell Me When to Go" and "Yay Area." No Valkyries player appeared to soak up the moment by the Bay quite like Williams. Somewhere between Mission and Brannan on the Embarcadero, Williams disembarked her double-decker bus along with Kiah Stokes with bottles of bubbly. After the Valkyries clinched the title on Saturday, Williams told her teammates to get excited for a true Bay Area experience at the parade. technology.title: Uber says it alone can make robotaxis pay, hours after Waymo quit its app
technology.description: Google-owned autonomous cab company Waymo has revealed it will stop allowing Uber users to book its robo-cabs, hours before the OG rideshare giant made a case for all autonomous vehicle fleet operators to use its platform instead of creating their own. This slow-motion fender bender played out across Wednesday, starting with Waymo Co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana telling Bloomberg that her company would end a partnership that saw it work exclusively with Uber in Austin and Atlanta. Mawakana said Waymo wasn’t happy about the fact that when users of Uber’s app requested a ride in one of its robo-cabs, they weren’t guaranteed to get one. News of that break-up came on the same day that Uber announced its quarterly results. As is common on such occasions, the company published remarks [PDF] its execs intend to make during an earnings call. CEO Dara Khosrowshahi used those remarks to promote the idea that Uber is the natural home for robotaxi fleet operators, because it already delivers around 30 percent higher trips per vehicle per day compared to apps run by autonomous cab companies. He said that higher utilization rate, plus use of shared charging and maintenance infrastructure, can deliver “higher fleet profitability even after paying Uber’s marketplace fee.” “As autonomous technology becomes more widely available, we believe this ability to commercialize vehicles profitably will become an increasingly important source of competitive advantage and value capture.” The two events are deliciously ironic, because Uber is arguing the scale of its platform makes it the ideal host for third-party players – just as Google does with its search, app store, and YouTube services. Left unsaid is that the two companies hold concerningly dominant positions in their respective markets. Khosrowshahi also outlined more ways Uber intends to strengthen its position, including by putting around 2,000 robo-cabs on the road in 2027, before “a much larger commercial ramp beginning in 2028.” That plan means Uber will run some cars itself and rely on third-party robo-cab operators who allow bookings on its app. “Importantly, building a broad ecosystem does not mean spreading our resources evenly,” the CEO explained. “We intend to maintain an open platform while concentrating capital, integration resources, and hands-on deployment support behind a smaller group of partners with the clearest paths to commercial scale and attractive economics at maturity.” Or in other words, as Uber uses more robo-cabs, it will try to maximize profits. Uber users booked $59.8 billion worth of services in its third quarter, up 20 percent year-over-year. The company recognized $14.75 billion of that as revenue, a ten percent improvement. Rideshare accounted for $29.5 billion of bookings and $7.5 billion of revenue. Delivery services brought in $5.5 billion of revenue on $28.5 billion of bookings. technology.title: Meta brings Conductor on board its model train
technology.description: Meta has acquired AI coding startup Conductor, signaling interest in applying AI to software engineering tasks. Charlie Holtz, the startup's co-founder and CEO, made the announcement in a blog post . He also revealed that the company's hosted Conductor Cloud, a sandbox for hosted agents, will go read-only on November 13 and shut down on November 20. Conductor , the eponymous company's macOS app for running multiple coding agents simultaneously in isolated copies of Git projects, will continue working for the next few months, and the biz expects to provide a way to transfer Conductor Cloud workspaces to local machines. But in early 2027, Conductor will no longer receive new models or critical bug fixes. A Meta spokesperson confirmed that the acquisition will strengthen the company's developer-oriented AI capabilities but declined to elaborate further. Perhaps Conductor will play nicely with Muse Code , Meta's recently introduced coding agent. Having spent heavily on strengthening its AI research lab , Meta has moderated its appetite for big acquisitions since April when China blocked its $2 billion offer for Manus AI , a developer of software agents. Meta's other acquisitions this year, Moltbook , Assured Robot Intelligence, and Stilla, are also AI-oriented but more modest in scope. The Conductor deal comes without an announced price, and follows in the footsteps of Meta regaining credibility as a model provider : Llama 4 disappointed but Meta's recent Muse Wonder and Spark models rank respectably among the top LLMs at the moment. In Meta's most recent conference call for investors [PDF], CEO Mark Zuckerberg said his company aims to provide AI agents that non-technical people can deploy for business tasks. "What we see is a lot of people are actually using Muse today to help run especially small businesses," he said. "And we think that there's both an opportunity to help create an agent that people use to really enable them to automate and do a lot of the parts of spinning up a small business that are just kind of difficult and time-consuming but aren't the core thing that a person is trying to do." Meta's AI strategy, as Zuckerberg describes it, is focused on collecting transaction fees from businesses for enabling agentic commerce, selling advanced AI capabilities to developers in the form of model access or tokens, charging for Muse to automate business tasks, and applying AI to personalize and improve results from ads. It's a good time to run an AI-related startup, as leading model companies seek to add value beyond offering AI models. Models themselves have become commoditized to the point that only a few leading model makers can get away with charging a premium. technology.title: Building AI factories at enterprise scale
technology.description: AI has become a juggernaut, driving technical strategy in the tech sector and outside of it. With the worldwide server market growing 30 percent in a single year to hit $122.6bn in the first quarter of 2025, IDC now feels safe recategorizing AI-driven investment "from cyclical to durable". The analyst company expects inference to account for over 70 percent of computing demand by next year, adding that it's growing fastest at the edge. Why enterprises are building their own All this investment in AI infrastructure might once have come mainly for hyperscalers, but that's changing quickly. Adoption is spreading quickly beyond public cloud service providers into enterprise environments, IDC adds. They're eager to run agentic AI in-house. There are plenty of reasons for companies to own their own AI infrastructure rather than offloading it to the cloud. One of these is data control, especially in regulated sectors such as finance, healthcare, manufacturing, and the public sector that have sovereign data requirements. Another revolves around the need for predictable costing from tokens delivered on tunable in-house systems. So what should companies look for in a supplier? Delivery speed will be a powerful driver for many who are under the gun to deliver AI initiatives for the business, especially during periods of constrained memory and CPU supply. Life cycle services will also come near the top of the list, for companies that need help managing everything from the power through to the reasoning LLM models and the workloads that use them. That need for expertise is unlikely to stop; companies will undergo changes in AI strategy as they get to grips with a still-evolving technology. From the desk to the datacenter ASUS expects this AI surge to continue in the datacenter, but elsewhere too, specifically in edge locations (especially industrial use cases) and at developers' desks, as the applications that will power the enterprise get made. It wants to be top of peoples' list for hardware and services at all these places along the AI continuum. At NVIDIA's GTC show in Berlin on Oct 21-22, it announced a full-stack AI offering that it's calling its Enterprise Agentic AI Solution . technology.title: Nintendo's biggest ROM chip supplier is bowing out of the business
technology.description: For years, the AI industry's insatiable demand for memory and storage has had plenty of knock-on effects on the price and availability of PC components like RAM , SSDs , and GPUs . Now those shortages are also squeezing the supply of ROM chips that power physical Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 game cartridges. Chip manufacturer Macronix announced in its third-quarter earnings report that the company's production of ROM chips "has reached its end" and that it will begin "gradually decoupling from the game industry," as reported by Taiwanese news site BigGo Finance . That could be an issue for Nintendo, which analyst David Gibson notes uses Macronix as its "main memory chip maker" for physical game cartridges. That ROM production—which has shrunk 39 percent in the last year and now represents just 5 percent of Macronix's business—is being crowded out by production of more lucrative, in-demand chips like NOR- and NAND-based memory and eMMCs, the company said. With Macronix's production capacity stuck at 25,000 12-inch wafers a month—and $1.2 billion in planned new capacity taking a year or more to spin up—less profitable ROM chips are taking up wafer space that can earn more through other types of chips. technology.description: Hackers possibly linked to the Kremlin exploited previously patched iOS and Android flaws in an attempt to hack visitors of multiple websites, including one celebrating the 250th anniversary of American independence, researchers said Wednesday. The attackers, which the researchers assessed with “moderate to high confidence” were part of Russia’s Foreign Intelligence Service, targeted other sites, many with links to that country’s ongoing war against Ukraine. The attacks began when iPhone or Android users visited one of potentially hundreds of different sites. JavaScript injected into the traffic then profiled the device. The final payloads, tailored to the type of platform visiting, attempted to steal browser cookies and, in some cases, Wi-Fi passwords and full mobile device data. Wielding DarkSword One of the impersonated sites was america250.org, belonging to a non-partisan group of lawmakers, business executives, and at least one former member of the Trump administration. technology.title: Uranium cubes reveal why the German nuclear project failed
technology.description: During World War II, physicists on the Manhattan Project worried that the Nazi German nuclear program might achieve the first nuclear bomb before the US and its allies. That's not what transpired, but historians have debated just how close the Germans came to achieving criticality in their last attempt at building a reactor: the B8 pile. Werner Heisenberg, who led that effort, claimed that they were close and had only needed a little more uranium. But according to a paper published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences Nexus, that was not the case: the project simply didn't have sufficient uranium and heavy water to build a working bomb, given the design they were using. This particular research started in 2013, when University of Maryland physicist Timothy Koeth—a co-author on the new paper—received the gift of a mysterious heavy metal cube from a friend. He instantly recognized it as one of the uranium cubes used by German scientists in their unsuccessful attempt to build a working nuclear reactor. Only 14 such cubes are known to exist today. In 2019, we reported on Koeth’s quest to track down the cube’s origins, as well as several other similar cubes that had somehow found their way across the Atlantic. At the time, Koeth and his partner in the quest, then-graduate student Miriam “Mimi” Hiebert, had tracked down ten such cubes around the US. For instance, the Smithsonian Institute had a German uranium cube in storage. They tracked a third cube to Harvard University, where it was regularly passed around to students in introductory physics classes as a curiosity. Read full article Comments

technology.title: Apple turns iCloud into spy cloud, will start looking at public share links
technology.description: If you share content using public iCloud links, Apple could soon be looking over your shoulder and checking for "harmful content." The iBiz announced plans to moderate publicly accessible iCloud share links in version 27.3 of iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and visionOS on a support page published on Tuesday. To clarify, this applies only to iCloud content shared via links created to be accessible to anyone, as opposed to content shared directly with other people. “Items shared using Anyone with the Link will be checked by Apple for harmful content,” Apple explained on the new help page without bothering to define what harmful content means. Based on the wording, it appears those checks will apply to all iCloud items shared using "Anyone with the Link," which Apple says it can also access. The company hasn't explained how the checks will work. The share-with-anyone option removes end-to-end encryption from the shared item, Apple said, even if Advanced Data Protection , Apple's optional end-to-end encryption feature for supported iCloud data, remains enabled for the account. “If you try to upload harmful content, Apple reserves the right to move, refuse, modify, remove, or delete the content at any time,” the help page continues, adding that the iMaker may also block or disable accounts associated with harmful content. The company also said it reserves the right to involve law enforcement when necessary, suggesting that its undefined "harmful content" category could include child sexual abuse material (CSAM), malware, and other potentially unlawful content. Without a proper definition of what it defines as harmful, however, iCloud users are essentially left at Apple’s mercy: If it chooses to continue to bend the knee to the Trump administration, for example, content deemed objectionable by the standards of political figures could end up wiped out. Apple also hasn't explained whether human moderators, automated systems, or both will be responsible for identifying and removing so-called harmful content, or whether any decisions will be left to AI, which can easily be fooled into making a bad moderation call. The scanning of such content, as mentioned above, begins with version 27.3 of Apple’s various OSes, which were released to developers in beta on Tuesday, with a general release expected in December. Apple didn’t respond to questions for this story. ®

technology.title: Hey, Siri: Plug into my app like you said you'd do way back in 2024
technology.description: As of Tuesday, developers can explore expanded Siri AI integration for their Apple platform apps through beta releases of iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, macOS 27.3, and visionOS 27.3. Next spring, nearly three years after announcing plans for deeper third-party Siri integration, Apple expects to begin accepting App Store submissions using the new capabilities. "This developer beta offers a sneak peek at Siri AI app intents for developers," Apple said in a developer news post . "With this early Developer Preview, your app can work directly with Siri AI, giving you a first look at new ways to reach and serve your customers." Anything is likely to be an improvement. Apple's Siri, a voice-activated assistant service, dates back to 2011 and gained limited third-party app access in 2016. In 2024, it became an interface for interacting with Apple Intelligence, its suite of generative AI features. Apple Intelligence has not been very intelligent – several advertised Siri capabilities were delayed, so much so that Apple was sued in 2025 over allegations of misleading marketing. After a shakeup of Apple's machine learning group in December 2025, Siri and Apple Intelligence received a makeover at Apple's Worldwide Developers Conference in June. "Before this year, Siri was a timer with a voice," said Roberto Gutierrez, Apple platforms staff engineer at a media company and author of the e-book On-Device Intelligence, in an email to The Register . "Weather, alarms, calls. Anything past that was a coin toss. "On the developer side, SiriKit covered a handful of domains and Shortcuts only worked if users memorized the phrase. Siri AI is the first version that understands context and can chain actions across apps. That's a real change." There is a catch, however, Gutierrez observed. Siri AI is available in a limited number of languages and regions. Support for Traditional Chinese is expected by the end of 2026, and EU availability remains a matter of negotiation – Siri AI is unavailable on iOS, iPadOS, and watchOS in the bloc as Apple works through interoperability concerns under Europe's Digital Markets Act. "Apple is working constructively with the EU in an attempt to find a path forward," the company said last month without committing to any concessions. Gutierrez said that he expects opening Siri to third-party developers will be useful to some extent. "Siri can only do what apps expose through App Intents, and SiriKit is on its way out," he said. "If your app's main actions aren't exposed, the new Siri can't see you. The bigger shift is letting Claude, Gemini and others plug in. Developers already choose between three options for every AI feature: Apple's system model, an open model through MLX, or a cloud API. Siri is heading the same way. science.title: NASA Announces X-70 Experimental Aircraft to Advance Flight Research
science.description: Generated image of NASA’s new X-70 Fractal experimental aircraft, a crewed, rapidly reconfigurable research platform for advanced aviation technologies. On Wednesday, NASA unveiled its newest experimental aircraft, the X-70 Fractal, during the UP.Summit at the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. This high-performance, highly adaptable research platform is designed to accelerate the development and testing of advanced aviation technologies. The crewed X-70 features advanced, rapidly reconfigurable flight-control technology that will allow NASA to explore aircraft maneuverability in ways never before demonstrated in crewed flight. The aircraft can also accommodate up to 2,000 pounds of experimental payloads in internal and external locations, enabling a wide range of research and flight-testing opportunities. “The X-70 Fractal gives NASA a crewed, high-performance platform to test advanced flight-control, maneuverability, and other cutting-edge technologies in real flight,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. “Its modular design and ability to rapidly swap internal and external payloads will keep our teams flying, learning, and moving quickly from one experiment to the next. We expect her first flight under the NASA banner within the next two years, and X-70 is just one part of this new beginning for aeronautics. This is why people come to NASA: to build, to learn, and most importantly, to fly.” The X-70 Fractal has a takeoff weight of 10,000 pounds and is designed to cruise at Mach .75, reach altitudes of up to 45,000 feet, and provide an operational range exceeding about 1,726 miles (1,500 nautical miles). These capabilities will enable NASA to conduct demanding flight research across a broad range of operating conditions. “For decades, NASA Aeronautics has used X-planes to develop technologies that advance aviation,” said Laurie Grindle, director of the Aeronautics Division within NASA’s Research and Technology Mission Directorate. “It’s exciting to bring on another X-plane to accelerate and drive aeronautics research.” The X-70 joins a storied legacy of experimental aircraft that have helped establish America’s leadership in aviation. From the Bell X-1, which first broke the sound barrier in 1947, to the X-15 hypersonic research aircraft and today’s X-59 quiet supersonic demonstrator, NASA has spent decades pushing the boundaries of flight. With the X-70, NASA will expand its capacity to conduct experimental flight research, accelerate the testing of emerging technologies, and advance the next generation of American aviation.
